title: Polynomial verification from polynomial-size wirings
statement: Let $L$ and $W$ be languages of bit strings, with $W$ decidable in polynomial time. Let $m:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, and for each $n$ let a wiring be a list whose entries are either a bit constant or one of the $n+m(n)$ input bits. Suppose there are natural numbers $b,j$ such that, for every $n$, the wiring length plus one and the total number $n+m(n)$ of input bits are each at most $b(n+1)^j$. If $x\in L$ exactly when some assignment to $m(|x|)$ witness bits makes the wiring output a string in $W$, then $L$ has polynomial-size fan-in-two circuit verifiers with polynomially many witness bits.
hypotheses_covered: $m$ assigns a natural-number witness length to each input length.
For each length, a wiring list over the input and witness bits is specified.
For every $n$, wiring length plus one is at most $b(n+1)^j$.
Membership in $L$ is equivalent to existence of an $m(|x|)$-bit witness whose wired output belongs to $W$.
